disclaimer: UAE tax rules changed materially through 2025/2026. From 1 January 2026 the VAT Law amendments (FDL 16/2025), the Tax Procedures Law amendments (FDL 17/2025), and the sweetened drinks tiered excise all apply, and a new AML law (FDL 10/2025) has been in force since 14 October 2025. The e-invoicing pilot went live on 1 July 2026; businesses with revenue at or above AED 50M must appoint an Accredited Service Provider by 30 October 2026 (Ministerial Resolution 66 of 2026). The unified late-payment penalty (Cabinet Decision 129 of 2025) took effect 14 April 2026. Always verify against the FTA and MoF portals before quoting figures.

qfzp.name: Qualifying Free Zone Person
qfzp.summary: Eligible free zone persons get 0% on Qualifying Income and 9% on the rest.
qfzp.saas_note: SaaS is NOT a Qualifying Activity. Most free zone SaaS revenue gets 9%, not 0%. This is critical for setup_advisor recommendations.
qfzp.de_minimis: Lower of 5% of revenue or AED 5,000,000

small_business_relief.name: Small Business Relief
small_business_relief.summary: Revenue under AED 3M qualifies for full relief through tax periods ending 31 December 2026.
small_business_relief.extension_status_note: As of July 2026 no extension has been announced. Relief ends for tax periods ending 31 December 2026 and standard corporate tax applies thereafter.

registration.waiver_announcement: April 2025: penalty waived if first return is filed within 7 months of the end of the tax period.

pillar_two_dmtt.name: Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax
pillar_two_dmtt.applies_to: MNE groups with consolidated revenue at or above EUR 750 million

registration_status.status: DMTT registration opened on the EmaraTax portal (reported mid-June 2026); no registration deadline announced yet and comprehensive filing guidance is pending. Verify with the FTA.
registration_status.first_return_note: First top-up tax return (for FY ending 31 December 2025) is expected due 30 June 2027 under an 18-month transitional window. Verify with the FTA.

sports_entities_exemption.summary: Qualifying non-commercial sports entities (international sports entities, sports entities, and supporting ancillary entities) are exempt from corporate tax retroactively from 1 June 2023. Conditions include recognition by the Ministry of Sports or competent authority and exclusive use of income and assets for the entity's objectives; entities must register and apply for the exemption with the FTA and file an annual declaration.

fta_service_fees.note: Cabinet Decision 174 of 2025 revised FTA service fees from 1 January 2026: new fees for Unilateral Advance Pricing Agreement applications, and the paid paper Tax Registration Certificate and Warehouse Keeper Registration Certificate replaced by free electronic certificates with QR-code verification.

guides_2026.note: June 2026 FTA publications: updated Corporate Tax Guide on Taxation of Family Foundations (CTGFF1, 10 June 2026), Education Sector VAT Guide (29 June 2026), and a Basic Tax Information Bulletin on Corporate Tax Losses (25 June 2026). Per secondary legal reporting; verify titles and dates on the FTA guides page.

changes: Reverse-charge imports no longer require self-issued tax invoices.
Carry-forward of excess recoverable VAT is capped at 5 years from the end of the tax period in which it arose; 2021 credits start expiring during 2026.
The FTA may deny input VAT recovery on supply chains connected to tax evasion where the recipient knew.
The VAT Law statute-of-limitations article moved into the Tax Procedures Law.

tax_procedures.name: Tax Procedures Law amendments
tax_procedures.law: Federal Decree-Law 17 of 2025 (amending Federal Decree-Law 28 of 2022)

audit_window.summary: The standard 5-year audit and assessment window is extendable up to 15 years for tax evasion or failure to register, and the FTA gets 4 extra years to complete an audit notified before the window expires.

refunds_and_credit_balances.basis: Refunds and credit balances are claimable for a maximum of 5 years from the end of the relevant tax period.
refunds_and_credit_balances.transition: Balances older than 5 years are claimable only until 31 December 2026 under a 1-year transition.

tax_procedures.excise_statute_of_limitations: Consolidated into the Tax Procedures Law; the Excise Tax Law's standalone limitation article was repealed by FDL 17/2025.

esr.name: Economic Substance Regulations
esr.warning: Do NOT promise ESR filing tools for current periods. The 9 Relevant Activities only matter for historical filings.

key_changes: Fines for legal persons raised to AED 5,000,000 to AED 100,000,000.
Tax evasion added as a predicate offence.
aml_cft.historical_note: FDL 10/2025 replaces the Federal Decree-Law 20 of 2018 regime; FDL 20/2018 remains relevant only as a historical reference for pre-October-2025 matters.
dnfbp_categories: Dealers in precious metals and stones

vara.name: Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority of Dubai
vara.applies_to: Virtual asset service providers operating in Dubai (excluding DIFC)

issuance_rulebook_2026.note: April 2026: VARA published its first dedicated Virtual Asset Issuance Rulebook guidance, covering fiat-referenced and asset-referenced tokens and banning anonymity-enhanced cryptocurrencies (AECs), alongside a formal virtual asset derivatives regime.

ubo.name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner
ubo.summary: All UAE companies must maintain a UBO register and file with their licensing authority. 25% threshold for direct or indirect ownership.

excise.law: Federal Decree-Law 7 of 2017 (as amended by Federal Decree-Law 17 of 2025)

sweetened_drinks_volumetric.model: Tiered volumetric excise by sugar content, replacing the flat 50% ad valorem rate on sweetened beverages.
sweetened_drinks_volumetric.exempt: Drinks under 5g sugar per 100ml, or sweetened only with artificial sweeteners.
sweetened_drinks_volumetric.certification: A MoIAT Emirates Conformity Certificate is required to evidence sugar content; uncertified drinks default to the high-sugar band (AED 1.09 per litre).

e_invoicing.name: UAE E-Invoicing
e_invoicing.model: PINT AE on a Decentralized Continuous Transaction Control and Exchange (DCTCE) 5-corner model; e-invoices exchanged via accredited service providers (ASPs) and reported to the FTA through EmaraTax
e_invoicing.status: pilot phase live: the MoF and FTA launched the pilot on 2026-07-01 (announced at the 26 June 2026 Sharjah awareness event) with a selected Taxpayer Working Group; voluntary adoption is open to any business from the same date

revenue_at_or_above_aed_50m.note: The go-live date is unchanged despite the appointment extension.

asp_register.status: 41 pre-approved eInvoicing Service Providers on the official MoF register; pre-approval under Article 15 of Ministerial Decision 64 of 2025, final accreditation under Article 16 still pending
asp_register.criteria_note: Accreditation criteria updated by Ministerial Resolution 56 of 2026: active Peppol-certified service providers that passed OpenPeppol conformance testing, with the PSP product operational for at least 2 years.

technical_docs.format: PINT AE XML (UBL-based) on the 5-corner DCTCE model

e_invoicing.scope_note: applies to B2B and B2G transactions; phased by revenue band

late_payment_penalty.name: Unified late-payment penalty
late_payment_penalty.basis: flat 14% per annum on unpaid tax, accruing monthly, unifying the late-payment penalty across VAT, Excise and Corporate Tax (replacing the previous escalating monthly model)
late_payment_penalty.note: confirm the exact accrual mechanics and any caps with the FTA
